title: Nigeria's constitution lists a Sharia Court of Appeal among the courts
summary: Nigeria's constitution lists a Sharia Court of Appeal among the courts.
body: The judicial list in the English text includes a Sharia Court of Appeal of the Federal Capital Territory, a Sharia Court of Appeal of a State, and Customary Courts of Appeal, alongside the High Court and other courts. The source says: "urt of a State; the Sharia Court of Appeal of the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja; a Sharia Court of Appeal of a State; the Customary Court of Appeal of the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja; a Customary Court of Appeal of a State; such other courts as may be authorised by law to exercise jurisdiction on matters with respect to which the National Assembly may make laws; and such other court as may be authorised" The constitution lists those courts. Listing them is not a statement that every case in Nigeria is decided under Islamic law. The same list includes other courts.
